page: Vultr voc-m-2c-16gb-100s-amd is a memory-optimized instance within the Optimized Cloud Compute family. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an AMD EPYC processor running at 2.0 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 2 shared vCPUs derived from 1 physical core with 2 threads, 16.0 GB of system memory providing 8.0 GB per core, and a bundled 100 GB NVMe SSD for local storage. No GPU is included in this configuration. The CPU supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512, including VNNI and BF16, and hardware-accelerated cryptography via AES and SHA_NI.

Benchmark data reveals a mixed performance profile. The instance achieves top-tier single-core CPU performance in stress-ng testing, alongside strong single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression speeds. However, multi-core CPU performance falls into the average range, and the Passmark CPU score is weak, placing in the bottom 25%. Memory performance is moderate, with average large-block read and write bandwidth, though cached small-block read bandwidth is weak. Tradeoffs are evident in database and web serving workloads; Passmark database operations, Redis SET operations, and static web serving throughput all register in the weak to poor categories. Large language model inference is also constrained, with text generation on a 7B model performing poorly at 5.0 tokens per second.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, this instance offers a high memory-to-vCPU ratio on shared hardware, making it a viable option for memory-intensive workloads that do not require sustained, dedicated CPU performance. The inclusion of local NVMe storage and a complimentary public IPv4 address adds value to the resource profile. It is best suited for memory-heavy but compute-light applications, such as caching layers, lightweight memory-mapped databases, development environments, and basic single-threaded data processing tasks.
